assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks with magic-wavelength trapping reached fractional uncertainties near 10^-18, a step change in how precisely time and frequency can be measured. Measurement precision limits what we can learn, so this is the kind of instrument-driven advance I weigh most heavily. It has opened relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and dark-matter searches, and underpins the coming redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the first strontium lattice clock. Ye's group pushed it to the 10^-18 regime with many-body clock physics and cryogenic systems. Both are indispensable and the pairing is clean. I recall Hall and Hansch were already recognised for the comb, so the clock itself is not covered by earlier prizes; I have not checked other groups, such as Lemonde or Ludlow, who may be argued for.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs now operate clocks at or below 10^-18 and compare them across continents. The interpretation is stable and the impact is demonstrated. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether others (e.g., Lemonde, Ludlow, Hinkley, Schiller) have contributions the committee considers decisive.
Whether the redefinition of the second is needed before the prize is justified is a timing judgment, not a scientific uncertainty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Single-NV-centre optical detection and room-temperature spin coherent control created a solid-state qubit and a nanoscale sensor. Magnetometry, thermometry and biological sensing, and quantum-network nodes built on it, show how the discovery enabled further fields. As a rare-earth-crystal person, I know the long road from optical spin readout to useful devices, and NV centres cleared it.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko made the first single-NV optical detection and coherent control. Lukin led the sensing and many-body/quantum-network extension. The credit is defensible but Lukin's work is partly a broader programme that overlaps with other candidates; the split between the foundational experiment and the later sensing work is not entirely clear. Others (e.g., Awschalom, Hanson, Budker) might claim a share.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed across many groups over two decades. Applications in sensing are real, though most are still in research use. Timely.
uncertainties: The prize configuration may exclude other major contributors such as Awschalom or Hanson, and overlaps with candidate B005.
Commercial or biomedical sensing impact is still emerging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattices with ultracold atoms turned Hubbard-type models into tunable, directly observable laboratory systems. The superfluid to Mott insulator transition and quantum gas microscopy gave single-site resolution measurement of many-body states. This is a new way of observing nature and has changed how many-body physics is tested.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch, Cirac) proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation; Greiner and Bloch carried out the Mott transition experiment and the microscope; Esslinger did the fermionic Hubbard work. Choosing three requires dropping Cirac, Esslinger or others, which is a real allocation difficulty. I picked experiment plus the key proposal.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely replicated, with many groups running quantum gas microscopes. Recognition is timely. Whether it has solved problems beyond reach of classical computation is still evolving.
uncertainties: A compound discovery: the theory proposal and several experiments could warrant different recognition.
Overlap with B032 and B034 on Cirac and Zoller.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED brought strong light-matter coupling, dispersive readout and microwave photon control to superconducting circuits, and it is the architecture of leading quantum processors. The measurement toolbox (QND dispersive readout, parametric amplification) is of lasting value. The 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, so the field has been honoured but cQED itself is a distinct step.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf wrote the 2004 proposal; Wallraff and Schoelkopf's groups demonstrated strong coupling. Girvin is credited in the list but I would drop him to keep three. Choosing three of four means one important contributor is excluded; the experiment-versus-theory split is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed, with industrial scale-up. Recognition is fairly timely, though possibly seen as overlapping the 2025 award.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 recognition and with Devoret's contributions, which are outside the credited names.
Practical quantum advantage is not yet established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theory predicted flat bands at the magic angle and experiment then found correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene. This opened an entire field of moire materials with tunable correlated and topological phases. The impact on condensed-matter physics is large and the experimental demonstration is clear and reproducible.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the continuum-model prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group did the 2018 experiments. The experimental credit is concentrated in one group, though Dean, Efetov and Young contributed substantial moire results that are not credited here. A fair three-person split is plausible but not unambiguous.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups since 2018. The interpretation of the superconducting mechanism is still debated, so some of the physics is not settled. Perhaps a little early, but the discovery itself is solid.
uncertainties: Other contributors (Dean, Efetov, Kim) are not on the credited list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry provides inertial and gravity measurements of very high sensitivity, with uses in tests of the equivalence principle, measuring G and alpha, gravimetry and potential gravitational-wave detection. It fits my belief that new measurement techniques drive progress. It also relates to the quantum sensing applications I know from WACQT.
assessment.attribution: Bordé's theory and early work, Pritchard's first atom interferometer with gratings, and Kasevich's and Chu's light-pulse interferometers are all decisive. Chu is not in the credited names, and he already shared the 1997 prize for cooling, so the configuration is uncertain and Schmiedmayer, also credited, could be argued instead.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a technique, with commercial gravimeters and field instruments. Fundamental-physics results are still at the level of precision tests, without a decisive new discovery.
uncertainties: Whether the prize rationale is a technique or a discovery.
Absence of Steven Chu from the credited names complicates attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller's proposal for trapped-ion quantum gates, and the subsequent experiments with high-fidelity gates, entanglement and small-scale algorithms, are foundational for quantum computation. Ion systems still hold the best gate fidelities. Wineland's 2012 prize overlaps conceptually, which reduces the novelty of the experimental side.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are clear for the proposal. Blatt led the key European experimental demonstrations, although Wineland (already a laureate), Monroe and Home also have strong claims, so the allocation of experimental credit is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed with commercial development. Part of the area was recognised in 2012, so it is a partial overlap.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize for ion control.
Double-counting Cirac and Zoller with B042 and B034.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Ti:sapphire laser and passive mode-locking made femtosecond pulses a practical tool across spectroscopy, nonlinear optics, combs and attosecond science. It is an instrument that enabled a great deal of other work, which I value. Original conceptual novelty is lower than for the discoveries above, and ultrafast optics has recently been recognised by the 2018 and 1999 prizes.
assessment.attribution: Moulton invented the Ti:sapphire gain medium; Sibbett's group demonstrated Kerr-lens mode-locking; Keller developed SESAMs. The three are credible and distinct contributions, but Spence and others involved in Kerr-lens work are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with widespread use for decades. Recognition could be considered very late, and the prize panel may view it as an enabling technology rather than a discovery.
uncertainties: Whether Nobel criteria accept a laser gain medium and mode-locking technique now that CPA was honoured in 2018.
Credit for Kerr-lens mode-locking is contested.
